1.mascotDialogue: An arrow in a directed graph means exactly one thing — you may go this way! She says nothing at all about whether you may come back.

2.mascotDialogue: Line 8 sets exactly one cell in the matrix. A directed edge, she only ever writes adjacency[u][v] — never adjacency[v][u].

3.mascotDialogue: Every arrowhead points one way. This particular loop happens to form a cycle, but each edge, tesoro, remains individually one-directional.

4.mascotDialogue: This is the most common mistake with directed graphs — treating a one-way arrow like she secretly runs both ways. She does not! The visual only ever draws the direction you truly set.
